cultural.vision_reason: A red cotton shoulder-cloth with khit-woven supplementary weft bands (naga diamonds, horse-and-rider, floral and 'S' motifs) is a classic handwoven textile type used across Thailand/Laos, consistent with the claimed Thai attribution.

physical.title: shoulder-cloth
physical.summary: A rectangular cloth, a shoulder-cloth, with identical woven patterning at each end.  Ground made from red tabby cotton cloth (paired warps and wefts); plain centre field.  Deep patterned bands of different widths at each warp end [circa 65 cms].  Widest band has a diamond pattern, each diamond formed from two pairs of naga (mythical snake) motifs.  Also a line of yellow horses with rider; small-scale floral motifs; bird, scrolling and 'S' motifs.  Worked in supplementary weft, 'khit', using mostly yellow cotton yarns, with some green and blue silk yarns.  Warp ends plied and knotted at end.
